repo.description:
## Impact

The Microsoft Outlook contact lookup and the Microsoft SharePoint v1 item update build an OData $filter string literal from an expression-bindable parameter without escaping it. A single quote in the value closes the literal and rewrites the query. Where a workflow binds untrusted input into those fields, the Outlook lookup returns the bound mailbox's entire contact list instead of one contact, and the SharePoint pre-write lookup can be redirected so the node writes the submitted field values onto a list item the workflow never intended, both within the scope of the stored credential.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 1.123.85, 2.44.1, and 2.43.5. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Audit active workflows that use the Microsoft Outlook contact `getAll` operation or the Microsoft SharePoint v1 item update/upsert operation and remove any bindings that pass untrusted external data into the affected parameters.
- Apply network-level controls to restrict access to webhook endpoints that feed into these workflows.
- Deactivate affected workflows until the instance is patched.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: OData $filter Injection in Microsoft Outlook and SharePoint v1 Nodes
